subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu DM sessions rebuilt after gateway restart — duplicate keys + maintenance pruning

question: Should Feishu direct DM sessions be protected by maintenance, and what validation or repair policy should OpenClaw apply to malformed or cross-app Feishu `open_id` session keys?
rationale: The remaining fix crosses durable session identity, retention behavior, and possible history migration; automation can show the source paths but should not choose the store-growth and compatibility tradeoff alone.

options.title: TTL-aware DM protection plus Feishu ID repair
options.body: Protect active direct DM sessions by age, reject or quarantine malformed Feishu `open_id` values at the Feishu boundary, and add doctor repair or migration for existing malformed keys.

options.title: Blanket-protect direct DMs
options.body: Prevent all direct DM session entries from maintenance eviction, accepting larger session stores to avoid context loss.

options.title: Keep workaround-only behavior
options.body: Continue documenting `per-account-channel-peer` for multi-account deployments and leave malformed-key cleanup to operators until stronger live proof is available.

recommendation.title: TTL-aware DM protection plus Feishu ID repair
recommendation.body: Protect active direct DM sessions by age, reject or quarantine malformed Feishu `open_id` values at the Feishu boundary, and add doctor repair or migration for existing malformed keys.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans core session maintenance and compatibility policy, and steipete has the strongest history signal on the central maintenance surface.
